# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 65 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 65 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_065_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 3 — The Shepherd of Punishment

**65:1** "Now then, the angel of punishment, to whom those who fall away from God are handed over — he torments every such person according to his deeds. Such is his torment: the one who sins receives many torments, and one who does not sin receives few."

**65:2** "How then does the angel of punishment torment the soul of the man who has sinned?" "He torments him," he said, "through all the sufferings that he is worthy to suffer in his life — various losses, and losses of money and goods, and various illnesses and many afflictions, and all sorts of adversities. For from all such things arise sufferings and diseases and various troubles."

**65:3** "These come about," he said, "not through any malice toward the person, but because the Lord wishes to save this man. The Lord loves him and hastens therefore to chastise him, so that this man may be purified of the great iniquity that is in him."

**65:4** "Now those who are servants of God and have God in their hearts — when they learn that they are being afflicted, they think about their iniquities and their evil deeds, and repent. And having repented, they live to God."

**65:5** "But the soul of the man who has nothing and has no power against the angel of punishment — he remains in his torments to the end of his days."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the purgatorial-corrective theology of the Angel of Punishment in Similitude 6.*
